landing.faq_q1: Is AWJ right for my business?
landing.faq_a1: If you sell, buy, and manage stock, branches, or a team, AWJ’s core covers accounting, sales, purchasing, inventory, point of sale, HR, and reports — and you switch on extra applications when you need them.
landing.faq_q2: Do I need to install anything?
landing.faq_a2: No. AWJ runs in the browser on desktop, tablet, and phone, in Arabic and English, in light and dark mode.
landing.faq_a3: Each company has a configurable roles table that decides what every user sees and does, and users can be limited to specific branches or warehouses. Each company’s data is isolated from every other.
landing.faq_a4: AWJ issues tax invoices with a QR code and provides a VAT report. The groundwork for e-invoicing phase two is built (sequential counters, hash chain, and signing); submitting invoices to the Fatoora platform is not switched on yet.
landing.faq_q5: Can I open an online store and an app?
landing.faq_a5: Yes. You build your store with the store experience editor on AWJ’s data, with cash on delivery or branch pickup, and design your app with the App Builder. Publishing to the App Store and Google Play and online card payments are on the way.
landing.faq_q6: Does AWJ connect directly to delivery apps?
landing.faq_a6: Not yet. Delivery-app orders are recorded today with the platform’s order number and followed in the Delivery hub and channel reports; direct connections are switched on per platform once its agreement is in place.
landing.faq_q7: Are point-of-sale control indicators an accusation?
landing.faq_a7: No. Indicators rank what to review first and explain why; they are not proof of wrongdoing. The decision stays with a human reviewer and is kept in a log.

salesSettings.require_return_source_on: Required — no return without a source
salesSettings.require_return_source_hint: A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail wants “no refund without a receipt”, while services issue standalone credit notes for negotiated settlements. Either way, a linked return can never exceed its invoice’s quantity or price — that limit cannot be switched off.
salesSettings.return_window_days_hint: Measured from the invoice date. “0” means no limit — the default. A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail publishes a fixed window, while contracting and long-term agreements have none. It does not apply to a return without a source document, which has no reference date.
salesSettings.enforce_min_sale_price_on: Enabled — block prices below the minimum
salesSettings.enforce_min_sale_price_hint: When enabled, a line’s net price below the minimum on the product card is rejected. An owner or authorised manager may override it only with a required reason stored on the invoice line for review.
salesSettings.allow_standalone_credit_notes_on: Allowed — credit notes without an invoice
salesSettings.allow_standalone_credit_notes_hint: A business policy, not an accounting rule. A credit note linked to a posted invoice inherits that invoice’s net amount, VAT and rate and can never exceed what was invoiced, together with returns. A standalone note has no such cap and takes its VAT rate from the default above, so enable it only for negotiated settlements that have no invoice.

inventorySettings.title: Inventory and product settings
inventorySettings.subtitle: Control product behaviour, tracking mechanisms, stocktaking and warehouse permits.
inventorySettings.detailed_tracking: Track products by serial number, batch number or expiry date

inventorySettings.policy_block_all: Stop operations when stock runs out, for all products

inventorySettings.policy_allow_quantity: Allow only for products tracked by quantity
inventorySettings.policy_allow_quantity_hint: Negative stock is allowed only for products tracked by quantity, not for those tracked by serial number, batch number or expiry date.
inventorySettings.negative_stock_hint: Choose how the system handles negative stock. The policy applies to sales invoices, point of sale and purchase returns.
inventorySettings.allow_warning: Allowing negative stock does double damage: the inventory account (1140) ends up with a credit balance although it is an asset, and the moving average is corrupted by every later purchase, so the cost of goods sold comes out wrong. Use the inventory diagnostic report to see the affected items.
inventorySettings.show_stock_quantities: Show total and available warehouse quantity for products
inventorySettings.show_stock_quantities_hint: When off, the quantity is hidden from the product list and the product card. This option affects no balance and no journal entry — display only.
inventorySettings.total_in_stock_hint: Determines how quantity is checked on sale or issue: total stock, or what is available after deducting reserved quantities. Not built yet — there is no concept of a reserved quantity in the system today, so total and available are one number.
inventorySettings.c_products_d: Control product behaviour, tracking mechanisms, stocktaking and warehouse permits.
inventorySettings.c_categories_d: Create multi-level categories to group items and make filtering in lists and reports easier.
inventorySettings.c_brands_d: Create any number of brands to classify items, simplify managing them and link them to reports.
inventorySettings.c_units_d: Define base units and conversion ratios so you can buy and sell products in different units.
inventorySettings.c_employee_warehouses_d: Assign default warehouses to employees to track their permissions, stock movements and permits.
inventorySettings.c_barcode_d: Set barcode preferences and formats for accurate scanning and weight-based pricing.
inventorySettings.c_fields_d: Add custom fields to capture extra data and show it on product pages, lists and reports.
inventorySettings.unit_base_hint: The stock unit — every quantity in the ledger is counted in it.
inventorySettings.unit_factor_hint: The factor is how many “{base}” make one unit. It starts at 2 and takes no fractions: a unit smaller than the base is handled by making the smaller one the base. Changing a factor later never touches a posted document — the line copies its factor when it is created.
inventorySettings.restock_sales_returns_hint: A business policy, not an accounting rule: retail puts sound goods back on the shelf, while restaurants and food shops never restock a return. Either way, the amount refunded to the customer is unchanged.
inventorySettings.restock_off_note: When off: returned goods do not enter stock and the moving average is untouched; their cost is posted to “5180 Inventory Adjustments” instead of “1140 Inventory”. You can override this per return on its creation screen.
inventorySettings.low_stock_notifications_hint: Notify product managers when a tracked item reaches its configured reorder level or below.
inventorySettings.out_of_stock_notifications_hint: Notify product managers when a tracked item's available quantity reaches zero or below.

security.title: Security & integration
security.description: Guidance based on actual platform behaviour — for safe key handling, signing and deduplication.
security.bearerBody: Send the key in the Authorization: Bearer header from your server only. Never place it in a browser, URL or repository; it is stored hashed and cannot be retrieved after issuance.
security.scopeBody: Give each key only the scopes it needs. Matching is exact: a read scope never grants write.
security.oneTimeBody: The API key and the webhook signing secret are shown once, at issuance or rotation. If lost, rotate it; it cannot be recovered.
security.rotateBody: Revoke any exposed key immediately and rotate a webhook secret on suspicion. The effect is immediate.
security.idempotencyBody: Every write requires a unique Idempotency-Key header (8–255 chars). Re-sending the same key with the same payload replays the original response; the same key with a different payload is rejected as a conflict.
security.requestIdBody: A request_id is returned in every response and in the X-Request-Id header. You may supply your own value matching the pattern and it is echoed back — useful for tracing.
security.rateLimitBody: When the limit is exceeded, 429 is returned with Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers. Respect the wait and retry with exponential backoff.
security.signatureBody: Every delivery is signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp, a dot, then the raw request body, using the subscription secret. Recompute it and compare to the v1 value in the X-AWJ-Signature header in constant time, and check the timestamp is within your tolerance.
security.dedupBody: Each event has a stable id retained across retries. Deduplicate on X-AWJ-Webhook-Id so you never process the same event twice.
security.replyBody: Respond 2xx quickly to acknowledge; any other status or a timeout is retried with bounded exponential backoff. Deliveries follow no redirects and time out quickly, so do heavy work asynchronously.

paymentAdjustments.panel_hint: Provider reserve and debit/credit adjustments: each request needs evidence and approval by another user, then is consumed by a posted settlement. A request moves no money.
paymentAdjustments.kind_hint_reserve_hold: An amount the provider withholds from the payout: lowers the bank net and is held as an asset at the gateway.
paymentAdjustments.kind_hint_reserve_release: Release of a previously held reserve: raises the bank net and cannot exceed the held amount.
paymentAdjustments.kind_hint_adjustment_debit: A non-fee provider deduction (penalty/dispute fee…): lowers the bank net and is expensed to provider adjustments.
paymentAdjustments.kind_hint_adjustment_credit: A provider credit (compensation/correction): raises the bank net and is credited to provider adjustments.
